title: CRLR/414/2022 of VIJENDRA SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 414 of 2022
Vijendra Singh ....Revisionist
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and Another ..... Respondents
Mr. Abhishek Verma, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. Lalit Miglani, A.G.A. for the State of Uttarakhand.
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
The instant revision is preferred against the
following:-
(A) judgment and order dated 29.06.2017,
passed in Criminal Case No.933 of 2013, State Vs.
Vijendra Singh, by the court of Judicial Magistrate/ Civil
Judge (JD), Kashipur, Udham Singh Nagar ("the case").
By it, the revisionist has been convicted under Sections
279, 304A and 427 IPC and sentenced as hereunder:-
(i) Under Section 279 IPC, Rs. 1000/- fine
and 3 months simple imprisonment.
(ii) Under Section 304A IPC, Rs. 3000/- fine
and one year simple imprisonment. And,
(iii) Under Section 427 IPC, Rs. 1000/- fine
and 3 months simple imprisonment.

2
It has also been stipulated that in case of default of
payment of fine, the revisionist shall undergo simple
imprisonment for a further period of 1 month.
(B) Judgment and order dated
25.06.2022, passed in Criminal Appeal No.149 of 2017,
Vijendra Singh Vs. State, by the court of 2nd Additonal
Sessions Judge, Kashipur, Udham Singh Nagar ("the
appeal"), by which, the conviction and sentence passed
in the case, has been upheld.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. Facts necessary to appreciate the
controversy, briefly stated, are as follows: on
24.10.2009, the deceased Pooran Singh was riding on a
motorcycle bearing registration no.UP-21J-6373 ("the
motorcycle") and was returning from Kashipur to his
house. As soon as he reached Nani Factory, a roadways
bus bearing registration no. UP-15AT-1259 ("the bus"),
which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner
hit the deceased at 2:00 in the afternoon, due to which
the deceased, Pooran Singh, sustained injuries. His
motorcycle was damaged. The incident was witnessed by
Naresh Kumar and Parshuram. The FIR was lodged
when the deceased was still admitted in the hospital.

3
Based on the FIR, the investigation was carried out and
the Investigating Officer ("IO") prepared a site plan. The
bus and the motorcycle, both were technically inspected.
The motorcycle was badly damaged, whereas, the front
bumper of the bus was pressed from its right side. The
inquest and post-mortem of the deceased were also
conducted. After investigation, a chargesheet was filed
against the revisionist under Sections 279, 304A, 427
IPC, which is the basis of the case. On 04.01.2010,
cognizance was taken and the revisionist was
summoned to answer the accusation under Section 279,
304A and 427 IPC. The accusation was read over to the
revisionist on 21.10.2010. According to the revisionist,
he has falsely been implicated.
3. The prosecution, in order to prove its case,
examined 7 witnesses namely PW1 Malkhan Singh, the
informant, PW2 Naresh Kumar, PW3 Gyan Chandra,
PW4 Satish Kumar, PW5 Mahesh Kumar, PW6 SI Sudhir
Kumar, the IO, and PW7 Sanjay Kumar Verma.
4. After prosecution evidence, the revisionist
was examined under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1973. According to him, he was driving the
bus on the date of the incident, but he did not hit the

4
motorcycle. According to the revisionist, when he
reached at the spot with the bus, by the time, the
accident had already taken place. The police made him
to stop his vehicle and implicated him, falsely.
4. After hearing the parties, by the impugned
judgment and order dated 29.06.2017, passed in the
case, the revisionist has been convicted and sentenced
as stated hereinabove. The judgment and order was
unsuccessfully challenged by the revisionist in the
appeal. Hence the revision.
5. Learned counsel for the revisionist would
submit that the prosecution has utterly failed to prove
the charge against the revisionist. It is argued that in
order to prove the charge under Section 304A IPC, first
and foremost, the prosecution has to prove that a death
has taken place. Secondly, it is the accused, who caused
such death and finally, the prosecution has to establish
that such death was caused by rash and negligent act of
the accused. He would argue that PW2, Naresh Kumar,
is a neighbour of the deceased. The bus was taken into
custody by the police on the date of incident itself, but it
was technically inspected on 26.10.2009. The bus does
not suggest that the accident took place due to collision

5
because it is argued that there are less sign of a head on
collision. The front bumper on the right side is slightly
pressed; there is no paint of the bus on the motorcycle
or of the bus on the motorcycle.
6. Learned counsel for the revisionist would
also argue that the motorcycle was technically inspected
on 09.11.2009, which is after a long delay. The
motorcycle was found damaged from its front side.
7. It is also argued that even otherwise, the
sentence is quite excessive. The revisionist has been
driver with the Roadways Department for a long. He is
60 years of age. This is the only act, which has been
attributed to him. He has three minor children to look
after. Therefore, he may be released on probation.
8. On the other hand, learned State Counsel
would submit that the sentence may be adjusted by
proportionately raising the amount of fine.
9. This is a revision. The scope is much
restricted to the extent of examining correctness, legality
and propriety of the impugned judgment and order.
Generally, appreciation of evidence, at this stage, cannot

6
be done, unless the finding is perverse or the finding is
not based on any evidence or material evidence is
ignored or irrelevant material is considered. The Court
proceeds to examine this matter accordingly.
7. In the instant case, PW1 Malkhan Singh,
the informant, has lodged the FIR. He has proved it. In
his cross examination, he has stated that the revisionist
had run away from the place of incident.
8. PW2, Naresh Kumar, has witnessed the
incident. According to him, he had witnessed the
accident taking place. According to him, when the
deceased reached near Nani Factory on his motorcycle,
the bus, driven in a rash and negligent manner, hit him,
due to which the deceased was injured. According to
PW2, Naresh Kumar, the driver of the bus had left the
vehicle and ran away. He also tells in the court that,
subsequently, he came to know that it is the revisionist,
who was driving the vehicle.
9. PW3, Gyan Chandra, is the witness of the
inquest. He has stated about it.
10. PW4, Satish Kumar, had inspected the
vehicle involved in the accident. He has proved those

7
reports. According to him he inspected the bus on
26.10.200. The front bumper of the bus was slightly
pressed from the right side. With regard to the
motorcycle, according to the witnesses, it was damaged
from the front side.
11. PW5, Mahesh Kumar, has also stated
about the incident, but he is not an eye witness.
12. PW6, SI Sudhir Kumar, the IO, prepared
the site plan. He got the vehicles technically inspected.
He has also proved some other police documents as well
as the charge sheet. He has stated that the revisionist
had surrendered.
13. PW7, Sanjay Kumar Verma, conducted the
post-mortem of the deceased on 27.10.2009. He has
stated about the injuries, which he could detect.
14. It is true that according to the bus
inspection report, its front bumper was slightly pressed
on its right side. It is also true that the witnesses have
not stated that there was some blood on any part of the
bus or the motorcycle. Perhaps, this appreciation may
not be done in the revision. The impugned judgment and
order passed in the case reveals that the court had

8
discussed about the condition of the bus and the
motorcycle. Para 19 of the impugned judgment dated
29.06.2017, makes detailed discussion on it. Not only
this, PW2, Naresh Kumar is the eye-witness. He has
categorically stated as to how did the accident take
place. Whatever material has been considered in the
case is relevant. It is the admissible evidence, which is
considered while recording the conviction and sentence
of the revisionist. It is not a case that the finding is not
based on any evidence. It is also not a case that any
material evidence is ignored or any irrelevant material is
considered. The court below has rightly passed the order
of conviction and sentence. It does not warrant any
interference.
15. In so far as the adequacy of sentence is
concerned, undoubtedly in criminal law, one of the
toughest tasks is to award adequate sentence. It should
not be based on misplaced sympathy. At the same time,
it should not be much harsh. A critical balance has to
be maintained. It depends on various factors including
the offender, the victim, the manner in which the offence
was committed, the gravity of offence, its implications
and other attending circumstance. The revisionist is a
driver in roadways department. It is a rash and negligent

9
act. The revisionist did not look back as to what had
happened to the person, who was hit with his vehicle. He
ran away leaving the bus at the same place. It is also not
his case that he was apprehensive of any assault or
attack by the onlookers or the other persons , who were
standing at the place of occurrence. Why he could not
have helped the victim? May be a timely intervention
could have changed the scenario. But all those are now
in the realm of speculation.
16. Having considered the entirety of facts, this
Court is of the view that interest of justice would be
served if the revisionist is sentenced to 3 months simple
imprisonment under Section 304A IPC, 1 month simple
imprisonment under Section 279 IPC, and one month
simple imprisonment under Section 427 IPC, the fine
remaining unaltered.
17. The revision is partly allowed. The
conviction of the revisionist is upheld.
18. The part of sentence is reduced as follows;
the revisionist is sentenced under Section 304A IPC to 3
months simple imprisonment, under Section 279 IPC to
1 month simple imprisonment and under Section 427

10
IPC to 1 month simple imprisonment. The fine shall
remain unaltered.
19. The impugned judgments and orders are
modified in terms of sentence as indicated hereinabove.
20. Let the lower court record, along with a copy
of this judgment be sent back to the court concerned.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 09.09.2022 Ravi Bisht
